newsitem.title: USA: Pa. 650 MW Homer City units shut, back by mid-week.
newsitem.headline: Pa. 650 MW Homer City units shut, back by mid-week.

text.p: Two 650 megawatt (MW) units at the coal-fired generating facility in Homer City, Pa., were shut for unplanned repairs, and expected to resume operation by mid-week, the operator said Monday.
"Two units (are) off at Home City...both with tube leaks," said a GPU Generation Inc spokeswoman.
Homer City's unit 3 which was shut Friday is scheduled to restart tomorrow, while unit 2, which was idled Sunday, is expected to start up Wednesday, the spokeswoman said.
The adjoining Homer City unit 1, with identical generating capacity, was running at full output, she added.
Pennsylvania Electric Co (Penelec) and New York Electric & Gas Corp each have a 50 percent stake in the Homer City units.
Both Penelec and GPU Generation are subsidiaries of GPU Inc of Parsippany, N.J.
